# <span id="aanchor65"></span> Liquid Quality Source Editor

## Source Analysis Tab - Source Analysis Detail Screen

The Source Analysis Detail screen is available when you double-click a Source Analysis grid row.

The source analysis detail grid will change based on the fluid service selection.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Hydrocarbon Sources">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Hydrocarbon Sources</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Hydrocarbon Sources">



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 823;height: 477;" />

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Base Information">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Base Information</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="Base Information">

- **Sample Date** - Date/time that the sample was drawn. This required field is used to determine which meter batch this sample applies to.

- **Product** - The hydrocarbon product name of the sampled liquid. If provided, this analysis will only be applied to meter batches with the same product designation.

- **Base Density Calc Method** - The method used to calculate base densities for this analysis (HC Properties, COSTALD, TP-2, REFPROP). HC Properties is the default method, which uses the constants given in GPA-2145. If the designated product is configured to use Table E (TP-27) or Table E Extended (TP-27 EXT), then “Base Density Calc Method” will automatically populate with the “Sample Density Calc. Method” set on the Product. The user can always select any option.

  The following table depicts the order of precedence used to set the “Base Density Calc Method”:

  | Product with Sample Density Calc Method Defined on Import/Edit | Base Density Calc Method Defined on Import/Edit | Base Density Calc Method Used |
  |:--:|:--:|:---|
  | Yes | No | Default Base Density from the Product |
  | Yes | Yes | Base Density Calc Method Defined on Import/Edit |
  | No | Yes | Base Density Calc Method Defined on Import/Edit |
  | No | No | Use HC Properties |

- **Pressure Base** - Pressure base of the stated mix properties.

- **Temperature Base** - Temperature base of the stated mix properties.

- **Set Relative Density by Range** - Specialty option that should only be used in consultation with Quorum.

- **Inhibited** - Indication that this analysis is inhibited. An inhibited analysis will not be applied to meters and will not be included in any averages. It is an inactive analysis.

- **Has Extended Analysis** - Indication that this is an extended analysis. Extended analyses may include up to 200 components. FLOWCAL uses extended analyses to calculate and update the extended combinations as shown in the Characteristics tab of the Liquid Analysis Editor.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Data Tabs">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Data Tabs</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="Data Tabs">

- **Mole %** - Displays component mole percentages.

- **Mass %** - Displays component mass percentages.

- **LV%** - Displays component liquid volume percentages.

- **Sulfurs** – Displays sulfur content in ppm.

- **Additional** – Provides fields for various mixture attributes including S&W amount, shrink and flash factors, and product specification limits.

  - **Extended Analysis** - For source analysis records that have full analysis, mole % provided for the individual components in aromatics and BTEX groups are summed and displayed. These fields are read-only.
  - **Aromatics** - BTEX and their derivatives. There are total 43 aromatics compounds in the full analysis supported by FLOWCAL.
    - Benzene
    - Ethylbenzene
    - Toulene
    - Xylenes (m-Xylene, p-Xylene, o-Xylene)
  - **Product Spec** - Users can manually enter percentages for these special interest components: Aromatics, Olefins, Carbon Monoxide, Hydrogen, Water, and Hydrogen Sulfide.
    - **Aromatics** - These fields are independent from the individual components that are part of the extended analysis. These fields are edited by users, not calculated by FLOWCAL.
    - **Olefins** - These read-only fields display the summation of Ethylene, Propylene, and Butylenes.
    - **H2S** - H2S content, expressed in percentage.

  

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 479;height: 328;" />

- **Sample** - The Sample tab contains fields relevant to the conditions and methodology of the sampling and the lab’s analysis of the sample. The Sample tab contains data on two sub-tabs:
  - **Sample Sub-Tab** - Contains information to identify the sample and the conditions existing at the time the sample was drawn.

    

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 474;height: 325;" />

    The following densities, determined at sample conditions at the time of the sample draw, are supported:

    - Absolute Density (in vacuum)
    - Absolute Density (in air)
    - Relative Density
    - API Gravity

    If any of these densities are provided, the sample temperature, pressure and gauge/absolute indicator are required and exceptions 3501 to 3503 may be generated if these fields are missing. Atmospheric pressure (exception 3504) is required if ‘Gauge’ is indicated.

    A sample density may be selected to be applied to a meter or ticket via the Source Assignment editor.

  -  **Analysis Sub-Tab** - Contains information on the analysis process such the name of the chemist performing the analysis and the instrumentation used.

    

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 487;height: 337;" />

- **Custom** – Eleven custom fields that users can label and used in any fashion.

  

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 426;height: 315;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Buttons">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Buttons</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="Buttons">

- **C6+ Extended**

  - **View mode** - This button shows the current C6+ properties from the Source’s characteristic
  - **Edit/New mode** - This button allows entry of C6+ properties as listed on a lab report. C6+ properties are required when a source analysis is set to "Use Extended Characteristics" on the Characteristic tab

  

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 337;height: 337;" />

- **Calculate** – Runs calculations for the current analysis.
  - If the current analysis is an extended analysis, calculate extended combinations.
  - Starting with mole %, calculate mass %, LV% and mix properties.
  - Missing and previously calculated values will be replaced. Imported and manually edited values will not be replaced.

- **Normalize** – Proportionately normalizes the current mole percent analysis to 100% and initiates calculations.

- **Exceptions** – Displays unresolved exceptions

- **Full Analysis** – Opens the Extended Analysis Detail screen.

  A full or extended analysis is a detailed analysis that includes components between and beyond the customary C1 – C10 components. FLOWCAL supports approximately 200 compounds as defined in GPA TP-17 (1998).

  Given the large number of fields on this screen, FLOWCAL has provided some options to help filter the data. By default, all components are shown in the grid. By selecting one of the radio buttons in the Show box, the user can narrow down the values displayed to the compounds included in a carbon group (C5 – C6, C7, C8, C9, C10 – C15) based on elution order. That is, selecting C7 will filter and display those compounds that elute after hexane (C6), up to and including heptane (C7).

- **New**

- **Edit**

- **Exit**

- **Print**

</div>
